title: SIGHUP: the configuration reload without an IRC client
description:
MARK'S CALL. Out of scope for mimid-1wgh.140.4, which put the
configuration reload behind IRC's REHASH.

crates/mimid-agent/src/main.rs installs SIGINT and SIGTERM and no
SIGHUP, and every other daemon reloads on SIGHUP. The reload itself is
now a type of its own (`crate::reload::Reloader`), so a signal handler
that calls it is a few lines and would give the operator the reload
without an IRC client at all.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. With `[jmap]` only and no `[irc]`
there is no REHASH, because the reload is reached through the IRC front
end. Such a daemon has no reload at all today.

WHAT IT COSTS. REHASH answers the user: a NOTICE per setting that
changed and 382, or a NOTICE saying what was refused. A signal has
nobody to answer, so the same `Reloaded` has to go to the log instead,
and the log line for a refused reload must keep carrying the
`ConfigError` variant's own wording and never the error's source chain,
which quotes the offending line of a file that can hold
`[tls.acme.acme_dns] password` (§7.38).
